question: How can reward models be evaluated on a harder, contamination-free, multi-domain accuracy benchmark whose scores predict downstream use in best-of-N sampling and RLHF?
hypothesis: An accuracy-based benchmark on unseen human prompts with best-of-4 format should correlate with downstream performance of reward models.
contributions: A challenging multi-domain RM benchmark on mostly unseen prompts (leading RewardBench models score 20+ points lower)
Controlled reward-model training experiments (base model, epochs, data) with actionable insights
Study of benchmark correlation with best-of-N and PPO
Finding that the best RM for RLHF depends on matching the policy lineage and prompt distribution

method.summary: Builds a 1,865-prompt best-of-4 benchmark over six domains (Factuality, Precise IF, Math, Safety, Focus, Ties) from unseen WildChat prompts plus manual ones, scores >100 reward models, trains 120 Bradley-Terry RMs in Open Instruct, and correlates benchmark scores with BoN (113 RMs) and PPO (17 RMs).
method.task: reward model evaluation (best-of-4 classification), with downstream BoN and PPO validation

datasets.name: RewardBench 2
datasets.size: 1,865 prompts (Factuality 475, Precise IF 160, Math 183, Safety 450, Focus 495, Ties 102); each with 1 chosen + 3 rejected (Ties: variable)
datasets.source: ~70% unseen human prompts from WildChat (Zhao et al. 2024); Safety from CoCoNot; Ties manual. Code Apache 2.0, data ODC-By (to be released upon acceptance)
datasets.preprocessing: Initial ~3,000 prompts, curated to 1,865 by manual verification; QuRater + topic classifier; Tulu 3 decontamination against twenty downstream evals, no overlap; factuality double-judged by GPT-4o and Claude Sonnet 3.7, ~30% discarded on disagreement

datasets.name: Tulu 3 8B preference mix
datasets.preprocessing: Flipped-preference variant used as noisy-label control

datasets.name: Skywork preference mix
datasets.preprocessing: Subsampling either mix degraded performance; both combined in full is best

datasets.name: BoN downstream tasks
datasets.size: 16 candidates per prompt; subsample of prompts from large evals
datasets.source: GSM8K, MATH, IFEval, AlpacaEval 2, BBH, PopQA, HumanEval+

models.name: Bradley-Terry RMs (120 trained)
models.init_from: Tulu 3 8B SFT/DPO/RL, Llama 3.1 8B Instruct, Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct, Llama 8B Base, Qwen 7B Base, Tulu 3 70B SFT, Llama 3.1 70B Instruct

models.name: >100 existing RMs / LM judges (113 in BoN study)

other.generative judges: two prompting modes, rankings and ratings (1-10), best reported

other.use: BoN generator and initial PPO policy

training.objective: Bradley-Terry preference loss for RMs: log(1 + exp(r(x,rejected) - r(x,chosen))); PPO for policy experiments
training.regularisation: PPO KL penalty beta=0.05 (also 0.0325 as check)
training.hardware: H100 GPUs; PPO 16 GPUs for 2 days each
training.compute: ~55,000 GPU hours total; 8B RM 64 GPU hours/epoch (~120 models); 70B RM 1,280 GPU hours (5 models); 17 PPO runs; eval ~30 GPU hours for 160 models

other.PPO: 17 RMs, same tokenizer as Tulu 8B SFT, prompts from Tulu 3 8B preference mix, best intermediate checkpoint reported

inference.decoding: BoN: 16 candidates then argmax reward; Math gold answers: 5 completions per model at temperature 1.0 with majority vote
inference.samples: BoN N=16 per prompt from Tulu 3 8B SFT
inference.prompting: Generative judges: rankings (pick best of 4) or ratings (1-10, ties scored 0.5/0.33/0.25)

metrics.name: Accuracy (best-of-4)
metrics.definition: 1 chosen vs 3 rejected, correct if chosen scored highest; unweighted mean over six domains; random=25%

metrics.name: Ties score
metrics.definition: weighted score of accuracy (all valid correct answers above all incorrect) and whether margin correct-vs-incorrect exceeds margin among correct answers

metrics.name: Pearson correlation
metrics.definition: RB2 score vs downstream BoN average / PPO
